title: Controlled stimuli reveal motion information in video Transformer features
summary: Under controlled motion stimuli, a statistical test flagged 28.7% to 92.1% of final-layer coordinate axes across the tested video Transformers, with zero flags in the frame-by-frame DINOv2 control. The study measured co-variation with specified motion profiles. Activation interventions gave mixed evidence that the flagged features drove model decisions.
ai_technology: VideoMAE; V-JEPA2; TimeSformer; DINOv2; sparse autoencoders
organization: University of Chicago; Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago

source_review.scope: v1 Methods §3–4, Table 1 and Appendix F

evidence.tested: The authors evaluated final-layer coordinates and learned sparse features on designed visual stimuli, with multiple-comparison thresholds and an image-encoder comparison.
evidence.unknown: Positive tests indicate some temporal dependence under these stimuli and definitions. Rates do not measure pure temporal-feature prevalence or identify a mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained video Transformers provided learned features whose activation covariances were tested under controlled motion stimuli.
